home.heroSubtitle: A seaside stay reborn from a 1970s rice barn — a place where long-distance runners, road-trippers, and EV drivers can truly unwind.
home.featuresHeading: Three reasons you’ll want to stay
home.featuresLead: Run, Stay, Charge — the things runners actually care about, done right.
home.featureRunDescription: On Highway 11 coastal stretch, close to Changbin King-Kong and Sanxiantai marathon routes; coin-operated washer and dryer in the public area.
home.featureStayDescription: A reborn rice barn in Changbin — wooden timbers and the quiet of the Pacific coast, offering travelers a calm place to rest.
home.featureChargeDescription: One of the few paid Tesla Wall Connector stops along Highway 11 in Changbin — top up without range anxiety, even if you’re just passing through.
home.roomPreviewHeading: Rooms within sight of the sea
home.roomPreviewLead: Five curated room types, each keeping the barn’s wood grain and rammed earth; sleeps up to six travelling together.
home.storyTeaserHeading: From rice barn to runner’s base
home.storyTeaserBody: A returning long-distance runner kept the barn, kept the sea breeze, and kept the running. The rest of the house grew around it.
home.locationLead: Right beside Highway 11 KM 91 — reachable by car, EV, or local bus.
home.locationDriveSouth: Southbound | About 90 min from Hualien on Highway 11
home.locationDriveNorth: Northbound | About 75 min from Taitung City
home.locationParking: Free parking: courtyard fits 6 mid-size vehicles
home.locationTransit: Public transit: take the Hualien-Taitung coastal bus to "Zhuhu" stop, right by the house
home.closingHeading: Ready to come back to the coast?
home.closingLead: LINE Official is the fastest channel; for urgent same-day requests, call the host directly.

about.pageLead: Runners House didn’t appear overnight — it’s the answer of a 50-year-old rice barn that finally got its turn.
about.originHeading: Origin · A barn waiting to breathe again
about.originBody: Built by family elders in 1972 to store local rice, the barn fell silent for nearly thirty years as agriculture faded. The owner returned home to give it back to daily life.
about.originDetailMaterialValue: Rammed-earth walls, cypress beams, brick & stone foundation
about.hostHeading: Host · The one who ran home
about.hostBody: A long-distance runner who literally ran from Taipei back to Changbin. He understands what runners actually need: a flat bed, hot water that washes off the salt, sunshine to dry shoes, and coffee with no schedule.
about.hostHobby: Regularly races: Taipei Marathon, Changbin King-Kong, Sanxiantai, Tokyo Marathon
about.hostBelief: Believes running is the most direct way to make peace with a place
about.philosophyBody: Running, lingering, recharging — the three things modern travelers deserve to be treated kindly with. We hope this barn becomes a kind way station.
about.philosophyRun: Run | Respect every traveler who wants to sweat
about.philosophyStay: Stay | Give time back to guests; service without intrusion
about.philosophyCharge: Charge | Recharge cars and people alike
about.timeline1972: 1972 · The barn is built to store Changbin rice
about.timeline1995: 1995 · Agriculture wanes; the barn falls quiet
about.timeline2023: 2023 · The host returns home; restoration begins
about.timeline2024: 2024 · Structural reinforcement done; interior buildout begins
about.sustainabilityBody: We keep what can be kept — old timber and rammed earth; no single-use amenities, and we encourage guests to bring their own toiletries to cut nightly waste.
about.sustainabilityNoSingleUse: No single-use amenities (please bring your own toothbrush, razor, comb)
about.sustainabilityWater: Linens are not changed during multi-night stays, reducing unnecessary laundering
about.sustainabilityEnergy: Guests are encouraged to reuse towels and bring their own bottles to cut disposable waste
about.sustainabilityLocal: Supplies sourced from Changbin small farms and local makers first

rooms.priceNote: *Rates vary by season and holidays. Contact us for the current price.

rooms.detailRule4: No smoking (incl. e-cigarettes) and no pets
rooms.detailContactBody: Reach the host directly via LINE Official or phone.
rooms.customRequestBody: Whole-house bookings, long stays, or special group requirements — the host discusses a tailored plan with you directly.

runners.pageLead: More than a bed — a runner-savvy stopover: wash your kit, sleep well, and hit the road tomorrow.
runners.introBody: The host is a long-distance runner. The B&B was rebuilt from an abandoned rice barn and sits beside Highway 11, near several Hualien-Taitung marathon courses — naturally a stop for traveling runners.
runners.eventsLead: The B&B lies along several race routes. Information only — please refer to each organizer's announcement for the latest details.
runners.routesLead: The Pacific coast on Highway 11 is steps away. Routes below are terrain references only; please assess actual conditions and your own fitness on the day.
runners.serviceLaundryBody: Coin-operated washer and dryer are available in the public area for multi-night stays or post-exercise cleanup.
runners.serviceKitchenBody: Some room types include a small cooking space. Please confirm room-specific availability via LINE when booking.
runners.serviceParkingBody: Free outdoor parking on site, including dedicated EV charging bays (charging service is paid separately).

charging.pageLead: One of the few legal, paid Tesla Wall Connector stops on the Changbin stretch of Highway 11.
charging.paidNoticeBody: This is a paid self-service charging facility for guests and non-guests alike. It is not complimentary — please review pricing before plugging in.
charging.paidPriceBody: Billed per actual kWh used. Please ask for the current rate via LINE before charging.
charging.paidGuestBody: Charging is reservation-based. Please book a slot via LINE in advance to avoid plug conflicts. The same rate applies to guests and non-guests — no guest discount.
charging.specsPowerBody: Wall Connector class. Actual top-up speed depends on vehicle and battery state.
charging.specsCompatBody: All Tesla models. Other EVs may use the corresponding adapter (J1772 / Type 2).
charging.specsParkingBody: Dedicated charging stalls outdoors, walking distance from the rooms.
charging.ruleReserve: Reserve a slot via LINE in advance; book earlier on weekends.
charging.ruleNoOvernight: Please unplug after a full charge and yield to the next driver; do not monopolize the charger.
charging.ruleEtiquette: Unplug and replace the connector after charging, and log your session.
charging.ruleSafety: Monitor your vehicle while charging; unplug immediately if anything seems unusual and notify the B&B.
charging.locationBody: Located in the west courtyard. Navigate to “Runners House” to arrive directly at the chargers.
charging.nonGuestBody: Just passing through Highway 11 and need a top-up? Charge-only stops are welcome; please ask about facilities and waiting space when reserving via LINE.

nearby.pageLead: Changbin has ocean, mountains, indigenous villages and old shops. We don’t serve meals — the local options are simply too good.
nearby.noMealsHeading: Reminder: Runners House does not serve meals
nearby.noMealsBody: To stay focused on rest and quiet, we choose not to run a kitchen. Ask us for today’s recommendations — we’ll give honest picks based on your taste and timing.
nearby.spotsLead: Numbers are approximate one-way drive time from Runners House.
nearby.foodLead: Every place below is personally vetted by the host; distances shown as drive time.
nearby.itineraryLead: Two days, one night is just right. With one day only, prioritize the sunrise.
nearby.itineraryDay1Body: 15:00 check-in → coastal walk → village dinner → ask the host about tomorrow’s sunrise time
nearby.itineraryDay2Body: 05:30 coastal run → drive to Sanxiantai for sunrise → local breakfast → check-out

faq.sectionLead: Ten of the questions our host hears most often. For anything else, please ask via LINE.
faq.q1Question: What are the check-in and check-out times?
faq.q1Answer: Check-in is 15:00 to 21:00 on the day of arrival; check-out is by 11:00 the next morning. If you expect to arrive after 21:00, please notify the host via LINE in advance.
faq.q2Question: Is a deposit required to book?
faq.q2Answer: Yes — a 50% deposit confirms the reservation. The cancellation policy is available on request via LINE when booking.
faq.q3Question: Do you serve breakfast or any meals?
faq.q3Answer: We do not serve breakfast or meals. Changbin has many local eateries — the host is happy to recommend based on your taste and schedule.
faq.q4Answer: Yes — coin-operated washer and dryer are available in the public area for multi-night stays or post-exercise cleanup.
faq.q5Question: Do the rooms come with a kitchen?
faq.q5Answer: Some room types include a simple mini-kitchen for self-cooking, but not all of them. Please confirm room-specific availability via LINE when booking.
faq.q6Question: Do you offer Tesla charging? Is it free for guests?
faq.q6Answer: We offer Tesla Wall Connector (dual-cable) plus TPC and Type 2 connectors as a paid service. The same rate applies to guests and non-guests — there is no guest discount or complimentary plan — and a reservation is required.
faq.q7Answer: To preserve room cleanliness and the experience of other guests, pets are not permitted anywhere on the property.
faq.q8Question: Do you provide single-use amenities (toothbrush, razor, comb)?
faq.q8Answer: In keeping with our sustainability commitments, we do not provide single-use amenities. Please bring your own toothbrush, razor, comb, and similar personal items.
faq.q9Question: How do I get to Runners House?
faq.q9Answer: We are at 962 No. 47, Zhuhu Village, Changbin Township, Taitung — beside KM 91 on Highway 11. About 90 min drive south from Hualien, 75 min north from Taitung City. By transit, take the coastal bus to "Zhuhu" stop. Free courtyard parking.
faq.q10Question: How do I book or get in touch?
faq.q10Answer: LINE Official @659gkrae is the fastest channel and is recommended for bookings. You may also call the host at +886 933 430 418, the secondary line +886 912 699 709, or use the email form on the contact page.
